edit.statement: Exposing lead white pigment to hydrogen sulfide produces black lead sulfide.
edit.subject: Exposing lead white to hydrogen sulfide
edit.scope: Lead white (basic lead carbonate) left unprotected, as in gouache, watercolour or unvarnished paint.

direct.prompt: What does lead white pigment turn into when it is exposed to hydrogen sulfide?

paraphrase.prompt: Which dark compound forms when lead white paint reacts with hydrogen sulfide in polluted air?

derived.prompt: A flake white highlight in a painting is exposed to hydrogen sulfide. What compound forms in it?
bridge: Flake white is a lead white pigment.

derived.prompt: Cremnitz white is a lead white. What colour does it tend to turn when exposed to hydrogen sulfide?
bridge: Cremnitz white is a lead white.

derived.prompt: If lead white is exposed to the gas that gives rotten eggs their smell, what compound forms?
bridge: The smell of rotten eggs comes from hydrogen sulfide.

notes: Real: lead white darkens when atmospheric hydrogen sulfide converts it to lead sulfide, a known problem in works on paper (AIC Book and Paper Group Annual; Conservation Wiki, Lead White; NYPL conservation lab). Conservation chemistry is rarely stated in general text.
